context: Accessible hive plot with 80 nodes on 3 structural axes (sources, connectors, sinks) and ~120 edges; node position encodes activity along each axis, node size encodes degree (connection count).
first_impression: A structurally honest network visualization with correct area encoding and data-driven size scaling, slightly brittle due to a hardcoded radial domain.
what_works: Node size correctly uses d3.scaleSqrt() against d3.max(nodes, n => n.degree) — area-proportional and data-driven. Data join uses a key function (.data(nodes, d => d.id)), preserving object constancy across updates.
what_doesnt: Radial position scale has a hardcoded domain [0, 100] rather than deriving it from d3.extent(nodes, n => n.activity), so the Scaling and Shift metamorphic relations would break if activity values shifted or exceeded 100. No missing-value handling is needed here (no line chart), but the hardcoded domain is the primary robustness gap.
